attributes.name: UT Stand-in Minecraft (26.1.2)
attributes.author: discovery@ut-pelican.test
attributes.description:
Disposable Minecraft Java 26.1.2 protocol stand-in used by the Unnamed Tracking Pelican
discovery experiments while Mojang/PaperMC downloads are blocked. Same config contract as the
upstream Vanilla egg: server.properties port rewrite, ")! For help, type " readiness, "stop".

script.install:
#!/bin/bash
# Stand-in install script. Same shape as the Vanilla egg, but downloads from the
# disposable local artifact host instead of launchermeta.mojang.com.
mkdir -p /mnt/server
cd /mnt/server
echo "Downloading ${SERVER_JARFILE} from ${ARTIFACT_URL}"
curl -fsS -o "${SERVER_JARFILE}" "${ARTIFACT_URL}"
sha256sum "${SERVER_JARFILE}"
if [ ! -f server.properties ]; then
  printf 'server-port=25565\nserver-ip=\nlevel-name=world\nmax-players=20\nmotd=Unnamed Tracking stand-in\n' > server.properties
fi
echo "Install Complete"

attributes.name: UT Luanti (Minetest 5.6)
attributes.author: discovery@ut-pelican.test
attributes.description:
Disposable Luanti/Minetest 5.6.1 server (Ubuntu archive build, Minetest Game 1.9) used as the
second game in the Unnamed Tracking Pelican adapter comparison. Differs from the upstream egg in
one way: no --terminal. With --terminal Luanti switches stdout to an ncurses UI, the readiness line
never reaches Pelican's console and the server stays "starting" (observed in E10). Without it,
stdin commands are not read, so stop is SIGINT (^C). The image is a local yolk (ghcr.io is blocked).

script.install:
#!/bin/bash
mkdir -p /mnt/server/worlds
touch /mnt/server/server.log
# Same minetest.conf essentials as the upstream egg (admin name, no server-list announce).
if [ ! -f /mnt/server/minetest.conf ]; then
  printf 'name = utadmin\nserver_announce = false\nbind_address = 0.0.0.0\nserver_name = UT Luanti test\n' > /mnt/server/minetest.conf
fi
echo "Install Complete"
